name: DocsMint
author: HiAi-gg
description: Cloud or self-hosted knowledge for AI agents: hybrid search, reranking, GraphRAG, scoped MCP tools.

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Search readable DocsMint documents with hybrid full-text and semantic retrieval, optionally filtered by folder and tag names. Requires read access and stays within the active workspace/category. Use search_knowledge_graph for graph relations from seed documents or get_related_documents for neighbors without a text query.

query.description: Text to search for; preserve the language and terms relevant to the user request.

folder.description: Optional folder UUID from list_folders to scope retrieval.

tags.description: Optional tag names as shown by list_tags; documents match when they have any supplied tag name.

limit.description: Maximum result count, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read an existing document by UUID with its content, metadata, and tags before editing or citing it. Requires read access in the active workspace/category. Use export_document when you only need the portable Markdown body.

id.description: UUID of the document, obtained from search_documents or list_documents, and visible in the active scope.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new DocsMint document when no existing document should be modified. Optionally set a title, initial Markdown content, and folder or category placement; an omitted title defaults to “Untitled”. Requires write access in the target scope. A category-scoped credential must create inside its configured category, by selecting that category or a folder within it. Normal creation schedules indexing asynchronously and returns the created document. Use update_document for an existing document.

title.description: Optional title from 1 to 500 characters; omit to use the API default “Untitled”.

content.description: Optional initial Markdown content; omit to create an empty document.

folderId.description: Optional folder UUID from list_folders; the folder must be writable in the active workspace or category.

categoryId.description: Optional category UUID from list_categories; omit or pass null to leave the explicit category unset. A categorized folder still supplies the document’s effective category; without one the document remains uncategorized. Category-scoped credentials stay bound to their configured category.

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Modify an existing document by UUID after reading its current state. Omitted fields remain unchanged; null folderId removes folder placement and null categoryId clears the explicit category, while a categorized folder can still supply the effective category. Changing title or Markdown content requires edit access, while moving placement requires write access in the active workspace/category. The server stores the prior content in version history and queues indexing when content or placement changes. Returns the updated document. Use create_document for new content.

id.description: UUID of the existing document, obtained from search_documents, list_documents, or get_document.

title.description: Optional replacement title, 1 to 500 characters; omit to leave the current title unchanged.

content.description: New markdown content for the document.

folderId.description: Optional destination folder UUID from list_folders; omit to keep current placement or pass null to remove folder placement.

categoryId.description: Optional destination category UUID from list_categories; omit to keep the explicit category or pass null to clear it. A categorized folder may still supply the effective category. Category-scoped credentials cannot move outside their configured category.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List readable documents in the active workspace or category with page-based results. Optionally filter by folder or tag; page defaults to 1 and limit to 20 (maximum 1,000). Use search_documents for text or semantic retrieval.

folderId.description: Optional folder UUID from list_folders to limit the listing.

tag.description: Optional tag UUID from list_tags to filter the documents.

limit.description: Number of documents per page, from 1 to 1,000; defaults to 20.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: List folders readable in the active workspace/category. Omit parentId to list root folders, or supply a parent UUID to list its immediate children as a flat list. Use create_folder to add a folder.

parentId.description: Optional parent folder UUID from list_folders; omit to list root folders.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a new folder in the active workspace or category scope. Requires write access and returns the created folder. A nested folder inherits its parent category; for a root folder, pass categoryId when using a category-scoped credential. Category-scoped credentials cannot create outside their configured category.

name.description: Non-empty folder name up to 255 characters.

parentId.description: Optional parent folder UUID from list_folders; omit or pass null to create a root-level folder.

categoryId.description: Optional category UUID from list_categories for a root-level folder. A nested folder inherits its parent category; category-scoped credentials cannot escape their configured category.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Save a named, retained snapshot of an existing document’s current content before a planned change. Requires edit access and adds an entry to get_version_history without changing the document itself. Use restore_document_version with the returned version ID to restore its content later.

documentId.description: UUID of the existing document, obtained from search_documents or list_documents and visible in the active scope.

label.description: Non-empty snapshot label up to 200 characters, for example 'v1.0-release'.

description.description: Optional snapshot note up to 1,000 characters; omit if not needed.

tools.name: get_version_history
tools.description: Read versions for an existing document, including saved snapshots. Requires read access and returns version IDs with content and timestamps; pass a version ID to restore_document_version when the user asks to restore content. This is read-only and does not change the document.

documentId.description: UUID of the readable document whose version history you need; obtain it from search_documents or list_documents.

onlySnapshots.description: When true, return only named snapshots and omit auto-saved revisions; omit or use false for the full history.

tools.name: export_document
tools.description: Render one readable document as portable Markdown and return a markdown string in the response object. Does not modify the document or include its complete metadata; use get_document to inspect the editable document.

id.description: UUID of the readable document to export, obtained from search_documents or list_documents.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List categories visible in the active workspace or category scope. Requires read access; a category-scoped credential sees only its configured category. Use this before create_document or create_folder when you need an existing category ID.

tools.name: create_category
tools.description: Create a new category for the active workspace. Requires workspace-level write access; category-scoped credentials cannot create categories. Returns the created category. Use list_categories to inspect existing categories.

name.description: Non-empty display name, up to 255 characters, for example Project notes.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: List tags visible in the active workspace or configured category scope. Requires read access; use returned tag IDs to filter list_documents and returned tag names to filter search_documents.

tools.name: get_related_documents
tools.description: Traverse graph relations from one readable document without a text query. Requires read access and returns related document IDs plus relation metadata. Use search_knowledge_graph to rank graph neighbors with query text, or search_documents for normal hybrid retrieval. Results stay in the active scope and may be empty when graph data is unavailable.

documentId.description: Document ID returned by search_documents or list_documents; it must be readable in the active scope.

limit.description: Maximum related documents to return, from 1 to 100. Omit to use the server default.

tools.name: search_knowledge_graph
tools.description: Search graph relations from one or more readable seed documents, optionally using query text to filter and rank related documents. Requires read access and returns seed entities plus relatedDocs. Use search_documents first to obtain authorized seed IDs; use get_related_documents for one-seed neighbors without graph search. Results stay in the active scope and graph data may be empty when unavailable.

query.description: Optional search text up to 2,000 characters to filter and rank graph-related documents; omit it to inspect relations without query filtering.

docIds.description: Between 1 and 50 document IDs returned by search_documents or list_documents; each seed must be readable in the active scope.

limit.description: Maximum related documents to return, from 1 to 100. Omit to use the server default.

tools.name: get_document_index_status
tools.description: Read indexing and knowledge-pipeline status for an existing document without starting work. Requires read access. Use after a save or refresh_document_index to check progress or failures.

documentId.description: UUID of a document returned by search_documents or list_documents; it must be readable in the active scope.

tools.name: refresh_document_index
tools.description: Queue an explicit reindex for an existing document; processing is asynchronous and the response acknowledges the generation. Requires write access. Normal content and placement changes schedule indexing when needed, so use get_document_index_status first and refresh only when a retry is intended.

documentId.description: UUID of the document to refresh, obtained from search_documents or list_documents and visible in the active scope.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Move an existing document to trash; this is a soft delete and does not permanently purge its content or version history. Requires write access in the active workspace/category. Returns {id, deleted:true}. Use only when the user intends to delete it.

id.description: UUID of the document to move to trash; obtain it from search_documents, list_documents, or get_document.

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Delete a folder while preserving its documents. Direct child folders and documents are detached according to the server folder rules, and reindexing is queued for affected documents. Requires write access in the active workspace/category. Returns {id, deleted:true}.

id.description: UUID of the folder to delete; obtain it from list_folders. This detaches, but does not delete, the documents inside it.

tools.name: delete_category
tools.description: Delete a category and detach its folders and documents without deleting their content. Requires full workspace write access; category-scoped credentials cannot delete any category, including their configured one. Returns {id, deleted:true}.

id.description: UUID of the category to delete; obtain it from list_categories using a workspace-scoped credential.

tools.name: restore_document_version
tools.description: Restore content for an existing document from a version or named snapshot returned by get_version_history. Requires edit access. The server saves current content in history, records the restoration, and queues indexing. Returns the updated document; it does not recover a trashed document or change folder/category placement.

documentId.description: UUID of the document whose content should be restored; it must be visible in the active workspace or category.

versionId.description: UUID of a version belonging to this document, from get_version_history. Use the version ID, not a snapshot label.

prompts.name: organize_workspace
prompts.description: Plan safe document organization using DocsMint categories and folders.

prompts.name: research_workspace
prompts.description: Research a question with hybrid search and GraphRAG while citing DocsMint document IDs.

resources.name: editor-guide
resources.description: Editor usage guide: read before update, preserve language and structure, refresh the index when needed.

resources.name: search-guide
resources.description: Search and GraphRAG guide: hybrid retrieval first, graph only from authorized document IDs.

resources.name: workspace-catalog
resources.description: Live scoped workspace catalog of categories, folders, and tags visible to the API key.

localizations.name: DocsMint
localizations.description: Cloud or self-hosted knowledge for AI agents: hybrid search, reranking, GraphRAG, scoped MCP tools.
localizations.summary:
Search, read, create, and organize the same documents you use in DocsMint. Choose DocsMint Cloud for the simplest connection, or connect a self-hosted workspace with the stdio bridge.

## DocsMint Cloud — recommended

1. Open [DocsMint Cloud setup](https://docsmint.com/mcp/connect?source=lobehub_mcp).
2. Connect to `https://docsmint.com/mcp` over Streamable HTTP; no server deployment or local process is required.
3. OAuth clients discover hosted authorization. Follow the [DocsMint Cloud setup guide](https://docsmint.com/mcp/connect?source=lobehub_mcp) for currently supported discovery and client-connection methods. Consent binds one-hour access tokens to a workspace, optional category, and scopes. Refresh tokens are not issued.
4. Clients using API keys can send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with a workspace-bound or category-scoped credential created in the authenticated browser UI.

## Self-hosted — advanced

1. [Install DocsMint with Docker](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint#quickstart).
2. Create an API key in your DocsMint browser UI.
3. Set `HIAI_DOCS_URL` and `HIAI_DOCS_API_KEY` in your MCP client's environment, then run the stdio bridge:

```sh
bunx --package @hiai-gg/docsmint@0.9.1 docsmint-mcp
```

The npm package connects to your existing DocsMint API with your API key; it does not install the application, database, or hosted Cloud OAuth server.

[Client configuration](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint/blob/main/packages/mcp-server/README.md) · [Docker images](https://hub.docker.com/r/vgalibov/docsmint) · [Deployment guide](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint/blob/main/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)

## What your agent can do

- Search documents with hybrid retrieval and GraphRAG.
- Read, create, update, and organize documents within the granted scope.
- Browse folders, tags, version history, and indexing status.

## Latest release: 0.9.1

Prepares the open-source stdio bridge for a Glama Server listing with a schema-valid GitHub maintainer claim and clearer API-key setup. The hosted DocsMint Cloud Connector remains separate. No MCP capability or database migration changed.

[Release notes](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint/releases/tag/v0.9.1) · [Current README](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint#readme) · [Full changelog](https://github.com/HiAi-gg/docsmint/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
